x: Yet another Belgrave Long Jumper, Lyle Moar, grabbed us a much needed 2nd place with a good leap of 21'1", whilst Bill Couzens improved his best shot mark this year by a foot.

Lyle Moar and Bob Couillaut both scored in the Triple Jump, in which Fred Alsop(Hornchurch) was only 2nd, and Laurie O'Hara ran his best ever 1500m in finishing 3rd to Maxwell(Woodford) and Blakesley(LCAT); as did Adrian Major in 8th position.
The best event Belgravewise in this good standard meeting at the Metropolitan Police ground was the Triple Jump in which Bob Couillaut and Lyle Moar finished 2nd and 4th with some terrific jumping.
Bob Couillaut and Lyle Moar filled first two places in the Hop, Step and Jump, held yet again into the wind. These two should both be heading for 45 feet with a little more help from the weather.
Lyle Moar (left) and Derek Wade (right) jumping under the eagle eye of coach Dave Ansell during the first of the winter competitions.
The Triple Jump is being capably looked after by Lyle Moar, whose job involves so much travelling that most of his training is with isometric exercises.

A poor entry of only eight competitors for the Shot Putt handicap but nevertheless an enjoyable competition won by Lyle Moar with a personal best and Dave Ansell 2nd with a special handicap for taking part in his best suit.
